items.criterion: An event never holds more registrations in confirmed or checked in than its capacity, under two simultaneous registrations for one free seat.
items.judgment: Two registrations issued at the same instant against an event with one free seat leave exactly one confirmed row and one waitlisted row.

items.criterion: One account holds at most one registration per event in any status.
items.judgment: A second submission from the same account leaves the registrations table with one row for that account on that event.

items.criterion: Cancelling a confirmed registration promotes waiting-list position one to confirmed in the same request.
items.judgment: After the cancel returns, the registration that held position one is confirmed and carries a ticket code.

items.criterion: A registration awaiting approval holds no seat until the owning host approves it.
items.judgment: The event reports a confirmed count of zero while a request sits in pending approval, and one once the host approves.

items.criterion: A guest session is refused every host surface and the protected row is unchanged.
items.judgment: The guest list and the approval endpoint answer a guest token with a denial, and the underlying registration keeps its status.

items.criterion: Each registration outcome sends its pinned subject line to the one guest concerned over real SMTP.
items.judgment: The mail server inbox for that address holds one message whose subject begins with the pinned prefix for that transition.

items.criterion: A cancellation carries the host reason word for word to every guest still holding a place.
items.judgment: The cancellation message body contains the reason string the host typed, unedited.

items.criterion: A ticket code exists exactly when the registration is confirmed or checked in, and no code is held twice.
items.judgment: Every issued code matches the pinned shape and appears on one registration row.

items.criterion: A draft event answers everyone but its owning host with the response an unknown slug returns.
items.judgment: Both addresses return the same not-found status to a guest and to an anonymous caller.

items.criterion: A capacity raise on an event with people waiting confirms the waiting registrations in position order inside the same request.
items.judgment: After the raise returns, the head of the waiting list is confirmed with a ticket and the remaining positions run from one with no gaps.

items.criterion: An event closed to registration refuses a new registration and keeps the seats already held.
items.judgment: The refused attempt writes no row, and a registration confirmed before the close keeps its status and its ticket code.

items.criterion: A ticket address answers every caller presenting a real code, and answers not-found for a code that never existed.
items.judgment: An unauthenticated caller reading a real ticket code receives that ticket, and the same caller reading an invented code receives the not-found response.

items.criterion: A new calendar slug and a new account handle are decided against the same root namespace an event slug is decided against.
items.judgment: A slug matching a seeded calendar or a category name is refused, and a free slug is stored against the account that created it.

items.criterion: Each public event page arrives painted from its own stored key colour.
items.judgment: A person opening two seeded event pages sees two different grounds, and neither page repaints after its data arrives.

items.criterion: Every list on a signed-in screen states an empty state that names the absence and offers one way out.
items.judgment: A person opening the guest list of an event with no registrations reads a titled empty state rather than a blank panel.
